title: Surface ledger row
description: One observable a detector can read. Rows are proposed into ledger/inbox/ and merged by the arbiter.

observable.description: Exactly how a detector reads this: a JS expression, HTTP header, or wire property.

category.description: Shard key. Carried over from resources/surfaces.json.

subsystem.description: Patch-ownership unit. One owner per subsystem prevents patch collisions.

verdict.description: spoof: value comes from the profile. inherit: host value is already correct. suppress: surface must not exist for this device. out-of-scope: requires a cited reason. escalate: unresolved, needs the arbiter.

profile_field.description: The profile key supplying this surface's value, spelled exactly as config/profile.schema.json declares it: dotted, with [] for an array item and * for an additionalProperties child. An array, sorted, when one surface is served by several keys at once; a single key is a string rather than a one-element array. scripts/check-schema-wiring.py requires every name here to be a declared key, so this field and the profile schema cannot drift apart unnoticed. Required when verdict is 'spoof'. A row whose surface has no declared key at all carries profile_field_exception beside it.

profile_field_exception.description: Why this row's profile_field names no key that config/profile.schema.json declares. Carried on the row rather than in an allowlist inside the checker, so whoever edits the row sees it, and checked by scripts/check-schema-wiring.py in both directions: a bad annotation fails, and so does one that outlived its problem once the key is declared.

reason.description: not-a-device-property: a deployment or launch choice that travels beside the device profile rather than inside it. conformance-target-only: measured for V3 comparison and deliberately not a loader input. whole-profile: the row is about the profile transport, not one field. undeclared: a spoof surface the schema declares no key for, so the surface stays inherited from the host until one is added.

evidence.description: A repository path, or 'path:token'. The file must exist and must mention the token, which defaults to the last dotted segment of profile_field; a segment nobody can search for, such as the wildcard, must name its token explicitly.

corpus_coverage.description: present: a corpus field holds it directly. derivable: computable from other corpus fields. partial: the collector captures part of the surface and a detector can read more of it, so the row can reach V3 only for the measured part — recorded separately from 'present' because a reference existing is not the same fact as the capture using it, and collapsing the two is how a row gets closed on a probe that could not see its own surface. absent: no ground truth — the row cannot reach V3.

process.description: Which process actually produces the value. Determines the plumbing path.

emitters.description: Emitter index ids this surface joins to.

coherence_edges.description: Coherence graph edge ids this row participates in.

catalogue_keys.description: Keys from resources/surfaces.json that this row covers, for catalogue entries the observable string does not name verbatim — prose titles such as 'Math Transcendental Function FPU Precision', and members of a family the observable names collectively. Purely additive: scripts/validate-ledger.py also credits any catalogue key that appears verbatim in 'observable', so this array is only for the pairings text matching cannot see. A key here that is not in the catalogue is an error, because it means the catalogue entry was renamed or never existed.

tier.description: T0 measured, T1 primary, T2 secondary, T3 inference. See docs/METHODOLOGY.md §3.

source.description: Corpus row id, Chromium path:line, spec section, or URL.

verification_tier.description: REQUIRED tier: the gate this row is measured against, and the depth of check its verdict asks for. Compare against achieved_tier. Not a release condition — nothing is withheld from a build for lacking a label.

achieved_tier.description: ACHIEVED tier: the highest gate this row has actually passed, in the same vocabulary as verification_tier (docs/METHODOLOGY.md, '## 10. Verification', subsection 'How far something has been checked'). achieved_tier at or above verification_tier means the row has been checked as far as it claims to need; scripts/validate-ledger.py computes that comparison and reports every row whose status disagrees with it. V0: the row validates and its patch applies to the pinned tree. V1: a translation unit carrying the change compiles. V2: the change is inside a full build that succeeded, launched and passed the smoke suite. V3: a profiled launch was collected and diffed against an eligible physical reference for this surface. V4: a live detector suite ran against it. ABSENT means nobody has measured it yet, which is the honest record for a row nobody has implemented — never fill it in speculatively, because an invented achieved tier is worse than a blank one. Any tier above V0 requires a patch: there is nothing to build otherwise.
achieved_tier.$comment: V3-C and V4-C from docs/METHODOLOGY.md are a separate compatibility scoreboard with its own schema, ledger/schema/compatibility-acceptance.schema.json, and are deliberately not members of this ordered vocabulary.

status.description: May only become 'resolved' on T0 or T1 evidence. T2 and T3 can open a row, never close one. HOW THIS READS AGAINST THE TIERS: status closes on EVIDENCE tier (T0 or T1), not on the V ladder, so 'resolved' does NOT imply the required verification_tier was reached. A resolved row whose achieved_tier is below its verification_tier means exactly that: closed on measurement of the surface, without the depth of check its verdict asks for. That is a legitimate and currently common state — 20 rows are in it — and scripts/validate-ledger.py reports it so it is visible rather than inferred. The converse is also legitimate: a row may meet its required tier and stay open, because a tier is a class of check while a row's verification is a specific observation at that class, and the mechanical tier does not establish the observation.

patch_id.description: Entry in patches/series implementing this row.
